## BUILDER CONTEXT
# Builder Profile — Sam

## Role
Solo founder and full-stack engineer. Building across multiple projects simultaneously.
Primary consumer of all generated specs — implementation guides must be self-contained.

## Active Projects (2026)
- **sam-plugin** — personal OpenClaw plugin (this project); wires agent to Sam's live systems
- **spec-doc** — this tool (Flask :3101 + Angular :4201); documentation-first dev methodology
- **humanize-me** — live Flask + Next.js AI humanizer; production at humaniz.me
- **Bubls** — Ionic + Capacitor mobile app (event discovery, Zürich); Angular + Flask
- **Trendfy** — wardrobai/trendfy.me; AI fashion photoshoot; kill date passed, status TBD
- **OpenClaw** — local AI agent gateway; runs claude-cli provider, Telegram-connected

## Stack Preferences
- **Backend**: Python / Flask (thin, ~150 lines, Blueprints, openapi.yaml-first)
- **Frontend (web)**: Angular (standalone components, signals) or Next.js 15 + shadcn/ui
- **Frontend (mobile)**: Ionic + Capacitor (iOS 16+, Angular)
- **AI**: Claude CLI (dev) → Anthropic SDK (prod); chain adapter pattern
- **Deploy**: Docker Compose → Coolify; single gunicorn + nginx pattern
- **Agent platform**: OpenClaw (local gateway, claude-cli provider, Telegram channel)

## Engineering Preferences
- Brain dump → AI structures it → ship. Minimal viable shape, not maximum abstraction
- Small focused modules with clear boundaries — no god classes, no god files
- Adapter pattern for all external services (AI, DB, storage)
- In-process state (module-level dict + threading.Lock) is fine for single-consumer async
- No speculative abstractions — build for the one concrete case that exists now
- Files under 200 lines; named exports; one component per file
- Build order: frontend with mock data first → Flask built to match the UI's API contract

## Known Constraints
- Solo developer — no handoff; guides must be runnable by one person end-to-end
- No Redis, no Postgres (unless Supabase via Flask), no external queue
- Claude CLI subprocess timeout: 3600s; Anthropic SDK: no practical ceiling
- OpenClaw workspace plugin system: skills first (SKILL.md files), graduate to full plugin when needed
- Telegram is the primary mobile interface — responses must stay under 4096 chars


## ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLES (non-negotiable — follow these patterns)
# Engineering Principles — Sam's Projects

Non-negotiable across all projects. When a brain dump contradicts a principle, the analysis step must flag it.

## P1 — Adapter Boundary
All external service calls (AI, DB, storage, HTTP) go through a single adapter module.
No feature code imports a provider directly. The adapter is the only file that knows which provider is active.
- spec-doc: `modules/chain/adapter.py`
- OpenClaw plugins: wrap external calls in a dedicated skill or tool wrapper

## P2 — Thin HTTP Layer
Route handlers contain no business logic. Handlers: validate input → call service → return response.
- Flask: `routes.py` handles HTTP only; `service.py` holds pure Python logic
- OpenClaw: skill files describe tool invocations; no inline logic

## P3 — Async 202 + Polling for Long Operations
Any operation > 30s returns 202 immediately with a job identifier.
A background thread does the work. A status endpoint lets the client poll until `done: true`.
No HTTP connection held open. No Redis — in-process state keyed by job/project id.

## P4 — No Speculative Abstractions
Build for the one concrete case that exists now. No generic runners for one consumer.
No base classes for one subclass. No registries for one item.
Three similar lines of code is better than a premature abstraction.

## P5 — OpenAPI-First (spec-doc)
`openapi.yaml` is the contract. DTOs are generated from it. Never hand-edit generated files.
Routes implement the contract — not the other way around.

## P6 — OpenClaw Plugin Principles
- Skills first: start with `SKILL.md` files (no build step, iterate fast)
- Graduate to `openclaw.plugin.json` package only when skills hit real limits
- References are the single source of truth — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills
- Agents are declarative descriptions, not imperative code
- Context files (`MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, `TOOLS.md`) are loaded every session — keep them current
- Boot hooks fire on session start — keep them cheap (no blocking I/O)
- Channel-aware: skills must adjust output format per channel (Telegram ≠ web UI)

## P7 — File Size & Structure
- Files under 200 lines (hard target, not a guideline)
- Named exports only (no default exports in Angular/TS)
- One component per file
- Build verification required before each commit (Angular: `ng build --configuration production`)

## Code Rules
- No direct push to master — always PRs; PRs target master; live is deploy branch
- Daemon threads only (`daemon=True`) — never block server shutdown
- Empty context strings handled gracefully — callers never crash on missing context
- `read_context()` returns `""` for missing files; `PromptBuilder.section()` skips empty content


## CONTEXT FROM EPIC (generated in prior step)
# 🎯 Epic: Thin API Phase 3

## Business Value

The current `ai.service.ts` hard-codes Claude instruction strings inside TypeScript and overloads a single `/api/ai/text/rewrite` endpoint to serve nine distinct user actions. Every prompt tweak — even a single word — requires a frontend deploy, and the frontend ships proprietary AI behavior logic to every browser. This violates the facade principle and slows iteration on the product's core differentiator: prompt quality.

Phase 3 collapses the 9-in-1 endpoint into flat, action-named routes (`/api/brainstorm`, `/api/expand`, etc.) with all instruction logic relocated to backend SKILL.md files. The frontend becomes a thin generated client — zero prompts, zero AI knowledge — produced from `openapi.yaml` via `ng-openapi-gen`. This unlocks rapid prompt iteration (backend-only deploys), removes ~960 LOC of dead Python (`text_prompts.py` + obsolete `task_gen.py` paths), and eliminates the entire hand-written `ai.service.ts` file.

The user is Sam (solo founder, single consumer of spec-doc). The ROI is velocity: brain-dump → spec-doc workflows depend on these eight text operations, and every prompt change currently costs a full-stack deploy cycle. After Phase 3, prompts ship as plain markdown edits.

## Scope

### What This Epic Covers
- **Flat action-named routes** – 8 new POST endpoints (`/api/brainstorm`, `/api/expand`, `/api/compress`, `/api/clarify`, `/api/simplify`, `/api/tldr`, `/api/bullets`, `/api/rewrite`) replacing the overloaded `/api/ai/text/rewrite`
- **Route prefix decision** – Resolve `/api/<action>` vs `/api/text/<action>` ambiguity from braindump; lock in `openapi.yaml` before any other artifact is written
- **Locked response contract** – `{ text, latencyMs }` for all 8 routes; request shape is `{ text }` plus optional `style` (rewrite) or `question` + `context` (brainstorm)
- **SKILL.md authoring** – Create missing skills for `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets`; confirm `brainstorm` and `rewrite` cover the followup + style cases
- **Generated Angular client** – `ng-openapi-gen` produces the HTTP layer from `openapi.yaml`; new `ai.service.ts` is a 3-line-per-method facade over the generated client
- **Followup brainstorm consolidation** – `/api/brainstorm` accepts optional `question` + `context`; SKILL.md branches on their presence (no separate endpoint)
- **Deletions** – `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/api/ai/text/generate`, `/api/ai/text/iterate`, `/api/ai/text/lint-braindump`, `/api/ai/text/review`, `text_prompts.py` (423 LOC), all hard-coded instruction strings in `ai.service.ts` and `app.component.ts`

### What This Epic Does NOT Cover
- ❌ **`bootstrap-project` / `generate-epic-guide` skill migration** — Deferred to Phase 4; routes stay as-is
- ❌ **`task_gen.py` deletion** — Gated on bootstrap migration; separate audit
- ❌ **`quality/` module** — Still in use by active routes; separate audit
- ❌ **`/api/ai/text/generate` replacement** — Removed outright; no successor
- ❌ **Auth, billing, project CRUD** — Untouched
- ❌ **Async job pattern (P3 202 + polling)** — Not needed; all 8 routes are synchronous (single Claude call, < 30s)

## Tasks

| # | Task | Dependencies | Parallel | Effort | Priority |
|---|------|--------------|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | **Lock OpenAPI Contract** | None | — | 0.5 day | High |
| 2 | **Author Missing SKILL.md Files** | None | with #1 | 1 day | High |
| 3 | **Implement Thin Flask Routes** | 1, 2 | — | 1 day | High |
| 4 | **Generate Angular Client & Replace ai.service.ts** | 1 | with #3 | 1 day | High |
| 5 | **Cutover & Delete Dead Code** | 3, 4 | — | 0.5 day | High |

## Success Criteria

- ✅ `openapi.yaml` defines exactly 8 text-operation routes with locked `{ text, latencyMs }` response shape
- ✅ Zero instruction strings exist in any `.ts` file (`grep -r "You are" web/src` returns no AI prompts)
- ✅ `ai.service.ts` is under 50 lines and contains no HTTP code (delegates to generated client)
- ✅ Each Flask route handler is ≤ 15 lines (auth → extract → skill call → return)
- ✅ All 8 actions verified end-to-end from Angular UI through SKILL.md to Claude response
- ✅ `text_prompts.py`, dead `/api/ai/text/*` routes, and old hand-written `ai.service.ts` are removed from the repo
- ✅ Followup brainstorm works through `/api/brainstorm` with `question` + `context` fields (no separate endpoint)
- ✅ `ng build --configuration production` passes; backend tests pass

## Related Documents

- [Analysis](./analysis.md) – Problems driving this epic
- [Solution Architecture](./architecture.md) – System design
- [Timeline](./timeline.md) – Status tracking

Design the solution architecture to fulfill the tasks and scope defined above.

## Chain Adapter

- `CHAIN_PROVIDER=cli` → subprocess `claude -p` (local dev + Docker)

## REFERENCE CODE (port from, not code in the target repo)
# Reference Code — Patterns to Port

These are real working patterns from sibling projects. When architecture says "port from references.md",
describe the shape to port — not the implementation detail.

## financing-plugin — Claude Code Plugin Structure

The gold standard for a well-structured Claude Code plugin.
Location: `~/Projects/financing-plugin-extracted/`

### Plugin Layout Pattern
```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json   # Plugin metadata + version
├── agents/                      # Specialised agents as flat .md files
├── hooks/                       # SessionStart hook (context injection)
├── references/                  # Convention references (single source of truth)
├── skills/                      # Skills — each a SKILL.md
│   ├── SKILL_MAP.md             # Master index of all skills
│   ├── feature-pipeline/SKILL.md   # Orchestrator skill
│   ├── feature-requirement/SKILL.md
│   └── dev-build/SKILL.md       # Dev tools
└── docs/                        # Spec-doc specs (Epic, Architecture)
```

Key rule: **references are the source of truth** — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills.
Skills read from `references/*.md`, never inline the same constraint twice.

### SessionStart Hook Pattern
The hook fires on every session start and injects live context into the agent.
No heavy I/O — just read files and compute a snapshot. Fast and deterministic.

### Skill File Pattern (SKILL.md)
```markdown
# Skill Name

## When to use
[Trigger conditions]

## What I do
[Steps the agent takes]

## Tools available
[Bash, Read, Write, etc.]

## Examples
[Sample invocations]
```

## OpenClaw Workspace Files — Context Injection Pattern

The workspace files already loaded by OpenClaw every session:
- `AGENTS.md` — session instructions (auto-loaded)
- `USER.md` — who Sam is (auto-loaded)
- `MEMORY.md` — curated long-term memory (auto-loaded in main session)
- `TOOLS.md` — stack + environment (auto-loaded)

Port pattern: new skills should reference these files rather than duplicating their content.
`SOUL.md` defines agent identity — skills can refer to it for tone/style.

## spec-doc Bootstrap Adapter — Async 202 + Polling Pattern

Already shipping in spec-doc. Port this pattern for any long-running skill:
1. POST trigger → return 202 + job_id immediately
2. Background thread runs the work
3. GET /status/{job_id} polls until `done: true`
4. In-process dict keyed by project/job id — no Redis needed

Location: `~/Projects/2026/spec-doc/api/modules/ai/routes/text.py` (bootstrap)
and `~/Projects/2026/spec-doc/api/modules/ai/routes/task_gen.py` (generate-task)

## Trendfy — Docker + Deploy Pattern

gunicorn config for Flask with background threads:
```
gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:3101 --workers 1 --threads 4 --timeout 900 --worker-class gthread
```
`--workers 1` required when using in-process state dicts (no cross-worker sharing).
`gthread` allows daemon threads to coexist with gunicorn.

## humanize-me — Flask Thin Layer Pattern

Flask as a ~150 line AI service boundary:
- All routes: validate → call AI adapter → return streaming or JSON
- No business logic in routes
- Supabase accessed only through Flask, never from frontend directly


## CONTENT ROUTING RULES (violations are failures)
- Status words (Done, In Progress, Completed) → ONLY in timeline.md
- Code blocks with implementation → ONLY in implementation guides
- Business value and market analysis → ONLY in epic.md
- Design decisions and tech stack → ONLY in architecture.md
- Step-by-step instructions → ONLY in implementation guides
- Problem identification → ONLY in analysis.md
- Cross-references MUST be bidirectional (if A→B then B→A)
- Always use "Solution Architecture" (not just "Architecture") in cross-references
## Your ONE Job
System design, decisions, trade-offs. NO code blocks. NO status.

## Output Format
OUTPUT ONLY markdown. Start with #. No preamble.

# Thin API Phase 3 — Braindump

## What this is

Phase 3 of the thin API migration. Phase 2 added the generic skill infrastructure (SKILL.md files, generic skill route). Phase 3 is about:

1. Clean, flat, action-named API contract — routes are `/api/brainstorm`, `/api/expand`, etc. No `/text/` or `/ai/` prefix.
2. Frontend becomes dumb — sends data, gets result, knows nothing about prompts or skills
3. All instruction complexity moves to the backend (Python route → skill → SKILL.md → Claude)
4. Angular API client generated from OpenAPI spec — no hand-written HTTP code in the frontend
5. Delete as much Python as possible — migrate all AI routes to skills, including `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide`

## The problem with the current frontend

`ai.service.ts` today has the brainstorm prompt instructions hardcoded in TypeScript:

```ts
brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextOperationResponse> {
  return this.rewrite(text, [
    'You are a product thinking partner. Given this raw brain dump, generate a structured brainstorm response...',
    '1. **Key Themes** — ...',
    ...
  ].join('
'));
}
```

This is wrong. Prompt engineering in TypeScript means:
- Prompts can't be improved without a frontend deploy
- The frontend is aware of AI instructions — it shouldn't be
- All the expand/compress/clarify/simplify/tldr/bullets variants are just `rewrite()` with different instruction strings baked in TypeScript

The fix: each action gets a named flat endpoint. The backend owns the instructions. Frontend sends `{ text }` and gets `{ text, latencyMs }`.

## Current API surface (frontend perspective)

### What the frontend actually calls today

**ai.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — used for rewrite, expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets, brainstorm, styleAs (all same endpoint, different instruction strings)
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — generic text generation with `{ prompt, tone }`

**projects.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project` — async spec generation (multi-step AI chain)
- `GET /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project/status/<job_id>` — poll bootstrap
- `POST /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide` — async epic guide generation
- `GET /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status` — poll epic guide
- `GET /api/projects` — list projects
- `GET /api/projects/<id>` — get project
- `POST /api/projects` — create project
- `PUT /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>` — save file

## Target API contract — flat, action-named routes

### Text operations (new — replaces the single /rewrite endpoint)

Each action is its own route. No `/text/` or `/ai/` prefix — just the verb. Backend owns all prompt logic.

```
POST /api/brainstorm   { text, question?, context? }  → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/expand       { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/compress     { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/clarify      { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/simplify     { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/tldr         { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/bullets      { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/rewrite      { text, style }                 → { text, latencyMs }
```

`style` values for `/rewrite`: Concise | Technical | Executive | Narrative | Punchy. Backend maps these to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what those instructions say.

No `/generate` endpoint — it's not used for a clear business action. Remove.

### Angular API client

Generated from `openapi.yaml` using `ng-openapi-gen`. No hand-written HTTP code. `ai.service.ts` is replaced by the generated client. Adding a new action = update openapi.yaml + add SKILL.md + add Flask route. Frontend regenerates automatically.

### Project management (unchanged)

```
GET    /api/projects
POST   /api/projects
GET    /api/projects/<id>
PUT    /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>
```

### Spec generation (migrate to skills in Phase 3)

`bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide` are multi-step async chains currently implemented in Python. Phase 3 migrates these to skill pipelines — the full chain (analysis → epic → architecture → timeline) runs via SKILL.md + agent, not Python service code. The endpoints stay but the Python behind them becomes a thin job dispatcher.

```
POST   /api/bootstrap          { project_name, braindump }  → { job_id }
GET    /api/bootstrap/<job_id>                               → { done, files, current_step }
POST   /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide               → { job_id }
GET    /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status        → { done, filename }
```

## Backend implementation

Each new `/api/text/<action>` route is a thin Python handler:
- Auth check
- Extract `text` from body (+ `style` for rewrite)
- Call the corresponding skill (which calls SKILL.md → Claude)
- Return `{ text, latencyMs }`

The skills already exist or need creating:
- `brainstorm` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `rewrite` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets` — may need SKILL.md files created

The Python routes are ~10 lines each. The intelligence lives in SKILL.md.

## What gets deleted

Once the new `/api/<action>` routes are live and the frontend is updated:

### Dead Python routes in text.py
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — replaced by individual action routes
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — removed, no equivalent needed
- `POST /api/ai/text/iterate` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/lint-braindump` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/review` — was never called from frontend

### Dead Python files (once routes and bootstrap are migrated)
- `api/modules/ai/services/text_prompts.py` (423 LOC) — all prompt strings
- `api/modules/ai/services/task_gen.py` (537 LOC) — most of it, once bootstrap is a skill pipeline
- `api/modules/ai/workflows/spec_gen/` — Python AI workflow chains replaced by skills
- Their test files

### Dead TypeScript
- `ai.service.ts` — replaced entirely by generated OpenAPI client
- All instruction strings, the `generate()` method, the base URL constants

## What stays

- `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide` routes (async, complex — Phase 4)
- `quality/` module (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- `task_gen.py` service (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- All auth, billing, project CRUD

## What the Angular service looks like after

```typescript
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class AiService {
  private readonly base = '/api/text';
  constructor(private http: HttpClient) {}

  brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('brainstorm', { text });
  }
  expand(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('expand', { text });
  }
  compress(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('compress', { text });
  }
  clarify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('clarify', { text });
  }
  simplify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('simplify', { text });
  }
  tldr(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('tldr', { text });
  }
  bullets(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('bullets', { text });
  }
  rewrite(text: string, style: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('rewrite', { text, style });
  }

  private post(action: string, body: object): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return firstValueFrom(
      this.http.post<TextResponse>(`${this.base}/${action}`, body)
        .pipe(timeout(AI_TIMEOUT_MS))
    );
  }
}
```

No instruction strings. No prompt logic. Each method is ~3 lines.

The `followupBrainstorm()` method in `app.component.ts` currently assembles context and sends a custom rewrite instruction. After Phase 3, this becomes a call to a dedicated `POST /api/text/brainstorm-followup` route, or the brainstorm skill handles the follow-up via the same `/api/text/brainstorm` endpoint with additional context in the body.

## Architectural principle — facade

The API is a facade. The frontend:
- Has zero instruction strings
- Has zero system prompts
- Has zero AI behavior knowledge
- Sends data, receives results

Every AI decision — what the prompt says, how Claude should respond, what context to include — lives in the backend. SKILL.md is the source of truth. Python routes are the facade surface.

This also resolves the followup brainstorm pattern. Currently `app.component.ts` assembles:
```ts
`You are a brainstorming partner. The user wants to explore: "${question}"
...`
```
That instruction string is eliminated. The endpoint becomes:
```
POST /api/text/brainstorm  { text, question?, context? }  → { text, latencyMs }
```
The SKILL.md decides what to do when `question` is present vs. absent. Frontend sends the data structure, knows nothing about what happens next.

Same principle for style/rewrite: frontend sends `{ text, style: "Concise" }`. Backend maps "Concise" to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what "Concise" means to Claude.

## Sequence

1. Create SKILL.md files for expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets (if they don't exist)
2. Add Python blueprint `/api/text` with 8 route handlers (thin, call skills)
3. Update `ai.service.ts` — new base URL, clean methods, no instruction strings
4. Test end-to-end
5. Delete old `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/api/ai/text/generate` routes
6. Delete `text_prompts.py` and its tests

## ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLES (non-negotiable — follow these patterns)
# Engineering Principles — Sam's Projects

Non-negotiable across all projects. When a brain dump contradicts a principle, the analysis step must flag it.

## P1 — Adapter Boundary
All external service calls (AI, DB, storage, HTTP) go through a single adapter module.
No feature code imports a provider directly. The adapter is the only file that knows which provider is active.
- spec-doc: `modules/chain/adapter.py`
- OpenClaw plugins: wrap external calls in a dedicated skill or tool wrapper

## P2 — Thin HTTP Layer
Route handlers contain no business logic. Handlers: validate input → call service → return response.
- Flask: `routes.py` handles HTTP only; `service.py` holds pure Python logic
- OpenClaw: skill files describe tool invocations; no inline logic

## P3 — Async 202 + Polling for Long Operations
Any operation > 30s returns 202 immediately with a job identifier.
A background thread does the work. A status endpoint lets the client poll until `done: true`.
No HTTP connection held open. No Redis — in-process state keyed by job/project id.

## P4 — No Speculative Abstractions
Build for the one concrete case that exists now. No generic runners for one consumer.
No base classes for one subclass. No registries for one item.
Three similar lines of code is better than a premature abstraction.

## P5 — OpenAPI-First (spec-doc)
`openapi.yaml` is the contract. DTOs are generated from it. Never hand-edit generated files.
Routes implement the contract — not the other way around.

- References are the single source of truth — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills

- Context files (`MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, `TOOLS.md`) are loaded every session — keep them current
- Boot hooks fire on session start — keep them cheap (no blocking I/O)

- Named exports only (no default exports in Angular/TS)
- One component per file
- Build verification required before each commit (Angular: `ng build --configuration production`)

- No direct push to master — always PRs; PRs target master; live is deploy branch
- Daemon threads only (`daemon=True`) — never block server shutdown
- Empty context strings handled gracefully — callers never crash on missing context

# 🎯 Epic: Thin API Phase 3

## Business Value

The current `ai.service.ts` hard-codes Claude instruction strings inside TypeScript and overloads a single `/api/ai/text/rewrite` endpoint to serve nine distinct user actions. Every prompt tweak — even a single word — requires a frontend deploy, and the frontend ships proprietary AI behavior logic to every browser. This violates the facade principle and slows iteration on the product's core differentiator: prompt quality.

Phase 3 collapses the 9-in-1 endpoint into flat, action-named routes (`/api/brainstorm`, `/api/expand`, etc.) with all instruction logic relocated to backend SKILL.md files. The frontend becomes a thin generated client — zero prompts, zero AI knowledge — produced from `openapi.yaml` via `ng-openapi-gen`. This unlocks rapid prompt iteration (backend-only deploys), removes ~960 LOC of dead Python (`text_prompts.py` + obsolete `task_gen.py` paths), and eliminates the entire hand-written `ai.service.ts` file.

The user is Sam (solo founder, single consumer of spec-doc). The ROI is velocity: brain-dump → spec-doc workflows depend on these eight text operations, and every prompt change currently costs a full-stack deploy cycle. After Phase 3, prompts ship as plain markdown edits.

## Scope

### What This Epic Covers
- **Flat action-named routes** – 8 new POST endpoints (`/api/brainstorm`, `/api/expand`, `/api/compress`, `/api/clarify`, `/api/simplify`, `/api/tldr`, `/api/bullets`, `/api/rewrite`) replacing the overloaded `/api/ai/text/rewrite`
- **Route prefix decision** – Resolve `/api/<action>` vs `/api/text/<action>` ambiguity from braindump; lock in `openapi.yaml` before any other artifact is written
- **Locked response contract** – `{ text, latencyMs }` for all 8 routes; request shape is `{ text }` plus optional `style` (rewrite) or `question` + `context` (brainstorm)
- **SKILL.md authoring** – Create missing skills for `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets`; confirm `brainstorm` and `rewrite` cover the followup + style cases
- **Generated Angular client** – `ng-openapi-gen` produces the HTTP layer from `openapi.yaml`; new `ai.service.ts` is a 3-line-per-method facade over the generated client
- **Followup brainstorm consolidation** – `/api/brainstorm` accepts optional `question` + `context`; SKILL.md branches on their presence (no separate endpoint)
- **Deletions** – `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/api/ai/text/generate`, `/api/ai/text/iterate`, `/api/ai/text/lint-braindump`, `/api/ai/text/review`, `text_prompts.py` (423 LOC), all hard-coded instruction strings in `ai.service.ts` and `app.component.ts`

### What This Epic Does NOT Cover

# Thin API Phase 3 — Braindump

## What this is

Phase 3 of the thin API migration. Phase 2 added the generic skill infrastructure (SKILL.md files, generic skill route). Phase 3 is about:

1. Clean, flat, action-named API contract — routes are `/api/brainstorm`, `/api/expand`, etc. No `/text/` or `/ai/` prefix.
2. Frontend becomes dumb — sends data, gets result, knows nothing about prompts or skills
3. All instruction complexity moves to the backend (Python route → skill → SKILL.md → Claude)
4. Angular API client generated from OpenAPI spec — no hand-written HTTP code in the frontend
5. Delete as much Python as possible — migrate all AI routes to skills, including `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide`

## The problem with the current frontend

`ai.service.ts` today has the brainstorm prompt instructions hardcoded in TypeScript:

```ts
brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextOperationResponse> {
  return this.rewrite(text, [
    'You are a product thinking partner. Given this raw brain dump, generate a structured brainstorm response...',
    '1. **Key Themes** — ...',
    ...
  ].join('
'));
}
```

This is wrong. Prompt engineering in TypeScript means:
- Prompts can't be improved without a frontend deploy
- The frontend is aware of AI instructions — it shouldn't be
- All the expand/compress/clarify/simplify/tldr/bullets variants are just `rewrite()` with different instruction strings baked in TypeScript

The fix: each action gets a named flat endpoint. The backend owns the instructions. Frontend sends `{ text }` and gets `{ text, latencyMs }`.

## Current API surface (frontend perspective)

### What the frontend actually calls today

**ai.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — used for rewrite, expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets, brainstorm, styleAs (all same endpoint, different instruction strings)
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — generic text generation with `{ prompt, tone }`

**projects.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project` — async spec generation (multi-step AI chain)
- `GET /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project/status/<job_id>` — poll bootstrap
- `POST /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide` — async epic guide generation
- `GET /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status` — poll epic guide
- `GET /api/projects` — list projects
- `GET /api/projects/<id>` — get project
- `POST /api/projects` — create project
- `PUT /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>` — save file

## Target API contract — flat, action-named routes

### Text operations (new — replaces the single /rewrite endpoint)

Each action is its own route. No `/text/` or `/ai/` prefix — just the verb. Backend owns all prompt logic.

```
POST /api/brainstorm   { text, question?, context? }  → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/expand       { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/compress     { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/clarify      { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/simplify     { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/tldr         { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/bullets      { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/rewrite      { text, style }                 → { text, latencyMs }
```

`style` values for `/rewrite`: Concise | Technical | Executive | Narrative | Punchy. Backend maps these to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what those instructions say.

No `/generate` endpoint — it's not used for a clear business action. Remove.

### Angular API client

Generated from `openapi.yaml` using `ng-openapi-gen`. No hand-written HTTP code. `ai.service.ts` is replaced by the generated client. Adding a new action = update openapi.yaml + add SKILL.md + add Flask route. Frontend regenerates automatically.

### Project management (unchanged)

```
GET    /api/projects
POST   /api/projects
GET    /api/projects/<id>
PUT    /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>
```

### Spec generation (migrate to skills in Phase 3)

`bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide` are multi-step async chains currently implemented in Python. Phase 3 migrates these to skill pipelines — the full chain (analysis → epic → architecture → timeline) runs via SKILL.md + agent, not Python service code. The endpoints stay but the Python behind them becomes a thin job dispatcher.

```
POST   /api/bootstrap          { project_name, braindump }  → { job_id }
GET    /api/bootstrap/<job_id>                               → { done, files, current_step }
POST   /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide               → { job_id }
GET    /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status        → { done, filename }
```

## Backend implementation

Each new `/api/text/<action>` route is a thin Python handler:
- Auth check
- Extract `text` from body (+ `style` for rewrite)
- Call the corresponding skill (which calls SKILL.md → Claude)
- Return `{ text, latencyMs }`

The skills already exist or need creating:
- `brainstorm` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `rewrite` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets` — may need SKILL.md files created

The Python routes are ~10 lines each. The intelligence lives in SKILL.md.

## What gets deleted

Once the new `/api/<action>` routes are live and the frontend is updated:

### Dead Python routes in text.py
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — replaced by individual action routes
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — removed, no equivalent needed
- `POST /api/ai/text/iterate` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/lint-braindump` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/review` — was never called from frontend

### Dead Python files (once routes and bootstrap are migrated)
- `api/modules/ai/services/text_prompts.py` (423 LOC) — all prompt strings
- `api/modules/ai/services/task_gen.py` (537 LOC) — most of it, once bootstrap is a skill pipeline
- `api/modules/ai/workflows/spec_gen/` — Python AI workflow chains replaced by skills
- Their test files

### Dead TypeScript
- `ai.service.ts` — replaced entirely by generated OpenAPI client
- All instruction strings, the `generate()` method, the base URL constants

## What stays

- `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide` routes (async, complex — Phase 4)
- `quality/` module (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- `task_gen.py` service (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- All auth, billing, project CRUD

## What the Angular service looks like after

```typescript
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class AiService {
  private readonly base = '/api/text';
  constructor(private http: HttpClient) {}

  brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('brainstorm', { text });
  }
  expand(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('expand', { text });
  }
  compress(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('compress', { text });
  }
  clarify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('clarify', { text });
  }
  simplify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('simplify', { text });
  }
  tldr(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('tldr', { text });
  }
  bullets(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('bullets', { text });
  }
  rewrite(text: string, style: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('rewrite', { text, style });
  }

  private post(action: string, body: object): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return firstValueFrom(
      this.http.post<TextResponse>(`${this.base}/${action}`, body)
        .pipe(timeout(AI_TIMEOUT_MS))
    );
  }
}
```

No instruction strings. No prompt logic. Each method is ~3 lines.

The `followupBrainstorm()` method in `app.component.ts` currently assembles context and sends a custom rewrite instruction. After Phase 3, this becomes a call to a dedicated `POST /api/text/brainstorm-followup` route, or the brainstorm skill handles the follow-up via the same `/api/text/brainstorm` endpoint with additional context in the body.

## Architectural principle — facade

The API is a facade. The frontend:
- Has zero instruction strings
- Has zero system prompts
- Has zero AI behavior knowledge
- Sends data, receives results

Every AI decision — what the prompt says, how Claude should respond, what context to include — lives in the backend. SKILL.md is the source of truth. Python routes are the facade surface.

This also resolves the followup brainstorm pattern. Currently `app.component.ts` assembles:
```ts
`You are a brainstorming partner. The user wants to explore: "${question}"
...`
```
That instruction string is eliminated. The endpoint becomes:
```
POST /api/text/brainstorm  { text, question?, context? }  → { text, latencyMs }
```
The SKILL.md decides what to do when `question` is present vs. absent. Frontend sends the data structure, knows nothing about what happens next.

Same principle for style/rewrite: frontend sends `{ text, style: "Concise" }`. Backend maps "Concise" to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what "Concise" means to Claude.

## Sequence

content.text:
# 🏗️ Solution Architecture: Thin API Phase 3

## Architecture Overview

The current AI text-operation surface is a leaky facade: a single overloaded endpoint (`/api/ai/text/rewrite`) absorbs nine semantically distinct user actions, while the frontend hand-assembles Claude instruction strings and ships them to the browser. Phase 3 inverts this — the HTTP boundary becomes the contract, every action gets its own URL, and prompt authorship moves entirely to backend SKILL.md files. The frontend is reduced to a generated client that knows verbs, not behavior.

The mental model is **one verb, one route, one skill**. Each action is an independently addressable resource with a stable request/response shape locked in `openapi.yaml`. Behind the URL lives a thin Flask handler whose only job is auth + dispatch into the skill registry. Behind the skill lives a SKILL.md file — the single source of truth for what Claude is told. The frontend never sees the instruction; it sees only the result.

The keystone architectural insight is **the openapi.yaml is the integration contract, not a deliverable**. Locking the contract first (Task 1) lets the Flask routes (Task 3) and Angular client (Task 4) be built in parallel against a frozen interface. Generated code on the frontend means the Angular service shrinks to a 3-line-per-method facade — adding a future action becomes "edit YAML, write SKILL.md, write 10-line route" with no TypeScript HTTP plumbing to touch.

## Design Principles

| Principle | Application |
|-----------|-------------|
| **P1 Adapter Boundary** | All Claude calls flow through `modules/runtime/chain/adapter.py`. New routes invoke the adapter via the skill layer — no provider imports anywhere in `routes/` or `services/`. |
| **P2 Thin HTTP Layer** | Each of the 8 Flask handlers is bounded at ≤15 lines: `require_auth → extract body → call skill → return JSON`. Zero conditional logic, zero prompt concatenation. |
| **P4 No Speculative Abstractions** | One concrete handler per action. No generic `TextActionRunner` base class, no shared `ActionDispatcher`. Brainstorm's optional `question`/`context` lives inline in its own route — it does not become a generic optional-parameter framework. |
| **P5 OpenAPI-First** | `openapi.yaml` is locked before any handler or client is written. DTOs are generated for both sides; hand-edits to generated files are forbidden. |
| **P6 Skills First** | Each action is backed by a `SKILL.md` file in `plugin/skills/`. Instructions live in markdown, branching logic (e.g. brainstorm with/without followup) lives in the skill body — never in Python. |
| **P7 File Size** | `ai.service.ts` ≤50 lines after replacement. Each Flask handler in its own thin function. `text.py` (today's catch-all) is split or deleted, not bloated. |
| **Facade integrity** | The frontend has zero AI knowledge: no instruction strings, no system prompts, no style-to-prompt mappings. `style: "Concise"` is a label the backend interprets. |

## Component Design

### 1. OpenAPI Contract (`api/openapi.yaml`)

**Purpose**: The single source of truth for the 8 text-operation routes. Drives both the Flask DTO layer and the Angular generated client.

**Shape**: Eight POST operations under flat paths (`/api/brainstorm`, `/api/expand`, `/api/compress`, `/api/clarify`, `/api/simplify`, `/api/tldr`, `/api/bullets`, `/api/rewrite`). Locked response schema `{ text: string, latencyMs: number }` shared across all eight via a `$ref`. Request schemas diverge minimally — most are `{ text }`, `rewrite` adds required `style`, `brainstorm` adds optional `question` + `context`.

**Why this shape**: Flat verb-only paths (no `/text/` or `/ai/` prefix) eliminate the routing ambiguity flagged in the braindump. The shared response `$ref` ensures any future shape change (e.g. adding `tokensUsed`) lands once and propagates to both sides.

### 2. Flask Routes Module (`api/modules/ai/routes/text_actions.py`)

**Purpose**: HTTP facade — the surface where the contract meets Python. Replaces the overloaded handler in `text.py`.

**Shape**: One Blueprint registered at `/api`. Eight handler functions, each decorated with `@require_auth`. Every handler does the same four things: pull JSON body, validate the minimum field set against the OpenAPI-derived DTO, dispatch to the skill layer, time the call, return `{ text, latencyMs }`.

**Why a new file**: `text.py` today carries the legacy `/rewrite`, `/generate`, `/iterate`, `/lint-braindump`, `/review` routes plus bootstrap polling. A clean module makes the deletion in Task 5 surgical — old file goes, new file stays. No partial cohabitation.

### 3. Skill Dispatch Layer (`api/modules/ai/services/skill_dispatch.py`)

**Purpose**: The bridge from a Flask route to a `SKILL.md` invocation. Resolves an action name to its skill, builds the input payload, calls the chain adapter, returns the result.

**Shape**: A small function — `run_skill(action: str, payload: dict) -> str` — that loads the matching `plugin/skills/<action>/SKILL.md`, composes a prompt via `PromptBuilder.section()`, and routes through `chain.adapter.generate()`. No registry class, no plugin loader — just a function that reads a file and calls the adapter.

**Why thin**: Per P4, there's exactly one consumer (the 8 routes). A registry abstraction earns its keep at three or more variant consumers; here a single function covers it.

### 4. Skill Files (`plugin/skills/<action>/SKILL.md`)

**Purpose**: The instruction source of truth. One file per action.

**Existing**: `brainstorm/SKILL.md`, `rewrite/SKILL.md` (verify coverage of followup + style cases respectively).
**To create**: `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets`.

**Shape**: Each follows the financing-plugin SKILL.md pattern — *When to use*, *What I do*, *Tools available*, *Examples*. The brainstorm skill internally branches on whether `question`/`context` are populated (covering the followup case eliminated from `app.component.ts`). The rewrite skill maps each `style` value to its tonal directive.

**Why per-action files**: Prompt iteration is the velocity unlock. Editing a markdown file and redeploying the backend (no rebuild, no frontend deploy) is the entire point of Phase 3.

### 5. Generated Angular Client (`web-ng/src/app/api/`)

**Purpose**: Replace hand-written HTTP code with `ng-openapi-gen` output driven from `openapi.yaml`.

**Shape**: A generator-managed directory containing one service per OpenAPI tag plus typed request/response models. Treated as build artifact — `.gitignore`'d or marked generated, never edited. A pre-build step (or explicit npm script) regenerates it from the YAML.

**Why generated**: Hand-written HTTP code is the carrier for the prompt-leak anti-pattern. Generation makes "frontend knows AI behavior" structurally impossible — there's nowhere to hide an instruction string.

### 6. New `ai.service.ts` (≤50 lines)

**Purpose**: Ergonomic facade over the generated client. Preserves the existing call sites in `app.component.ts` so component code doesn't churn.

**Shape**: 8 methods (`brainstorm`, `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets`, `rewrite`), each ~3 lines: take args → call generated client method → return promise. No HTTP code, no URL construction, no headers, no instruction strings.

**Why a wrapper rather than direct generated-client usage**: The generated client surface is verbose (`TextOperationsService.brainstormPost(...)`); the wrapper preserves the readable call sites and absorbs any future contract drift in one file. Cost is ~30 lines of boilerplate; benefit is no churn in feature components.

### 7. Followup Brainstorm Consolidation

**Purpose**: Eliminate the instruction string assembled in `app.component.ts.followupBrainstorm()`.

**Shape**: The same `/api/brainstorm` endpoint absorbs the followup case via optional `question` and `context` body fields. The brainstorm `SKILL.md` decides what to render based on which fields are populated. No `/brainstorm-followup` endpoint, no second handler.

**Why one endpoint not two**: Adding a route for what is structurally "brainstorm with more context" violates P4. The shape difference is two optional fields; a second URL would imply two skills, two SKILL.md files, two handlers — three layers of duplication for one conditional branch.

## Technology Stack

| Layer | Choice | Rationale |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| Contract | `openapi.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.0) | Already present in repo; drives generation on both sides; mandated by P5 |
| Frontend HTTP | `ng-openapi-gen` (Angular 17) | Eliminates hand-written HTTP; structurally prevents prompt strings in TS |
| Frontend facade | `ai.service.ts` (signals-compatible) | Preserves existing call sites; absorbs generator verbosity |
| Backend HTTP | Flask Blueprint | Matches existing pattern in `modules/ai/routes/`; thin per P2 |
| Skill storage | `plugin/skills/<action>/SKILL.md` | Plain markdown; backend-only deploy iteration; matches OpenClaw + financing-plugin pattern (P6) |
| AI dispatch | `modules/runtime/chain/adapter.py` | Sole AI boundary per P1; reused unchanged |
| Auth | `require_auth` decorator (existing) | Reused unchanged from current routes |
| Job model | Synchronous request/response | All 8 actions are single Claude calls, well under 30s — P3 async pattern not needed |

## Design Decisions

| Decision | Rationale | Trade-offs |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| **Flat `/api/<action>` paths (no `/text/` prefix)** | Resolves braindump ambiguity; shorter URLs; verbs read as actions not categories. The route prefix collision with future non-text actions (e.g. an image action named `expand`) is unlikely given specview's scope. | Loses the "text namespace" grouping; if a non-text action ever shares a verb name, would need disambiguation. Acceptable for solo-use tool. |
| **OpenAPI-first, contract locked before code** | Allows Tasks 3 (Flask routes) and 4 (Angular client) to run in parallel against a frozen interface; halves the critical path; structurally enforces P5. | Demands discipline — no "we'll just add a field" mid-implementation. Schema drift requires re-running both generators. |
| **One handler per action, no generic dispatcher** | P4 — three near-identical 10-line handlers beat a 40-line abstraction with one concrete consumer. Each handler stays inspectable and grep-able. | Slight repetition (8 handlers vs 1). Mitigated by handlers being trivial; complexity shifts to the skill layer where it belongs. |
| **Generated client + thin hand-written facade** | Generator output is verbose and version-coupled; facade absorbs that churn and keeps existing component call sites stable. | Two layers of indirection (component → facade → generated client). Cost is one extra method definition per action; benefit is no component refactor. |
| **Brainstorm followup via optional fields, not new route** | Same skill, same response shape, just more context. A second URL would multiply files (route + DTO + skill) for one conditional branch — pure P4 violation. | Couples two use-cases at the URL level; if their SKILL.md instructions ever diverge significantly, may need split later. Reversible. |
| **Synchronous (no 202 + polling)** | Single Claude call per action, all observed under 30s. P3's async pattern is for chains and bootstraps, not single-shot rewrites. | If response time degrades (e.g. larger context, slower model), would need migration to async. Tracked separately. |
| **Delete `text_prompts.py` (423 LOC) outright, not deprecate** | All instructions migrate to SKILL.md; keeping a parallel Python copy guarantees drift. Deletion enforces the "skills are source of truth" rule structurally. | No fallback if a skill file is missing — but that's the desired failure mode (loud error vs silent stale prompt). |
| **`/api/ai/text/generate` removed with no successor** | No frontend caller, no clear product action. Phase 3 is the right moment to amputate. | Any future "freeform generate" need will require a new contract. Acceptable — generic generators tend to grow into messes. |
| **Bootstrap + epic-guide migration deferred to Phase 4** | They use the async 202 + polling pattern and sit on `task_gen.py` / `workflows/spec_gen/` — too much surface area to absorb without expanding scope. Phase 3 stays scoped to the synchronous text 8. | `text_prompts.py` and `task_gen.py` partially overlap; some prompt code stays alive longer than ideal. Documented as Phase 4 cleanup. |
| **Keep `quality/` module untouched** | Used by routes outside the 8-action surface; out of scope per epic. | Risk of `quality/` referencing soon-to-be-deleted `text_prompts.py` — mitigated by Task 5 audit before deletion. |

## Architectural Boundaries

The Phase 3 system has four hard boundaries, each enforced by a single principle:

- **HTTP ↔ business**: enforced by P2 — handlers are inspectable thin functions, business logic is unreachable from a curl request without going through the skill layer.
- **Frontend ↔ AI**: enforced by P5 + generated client — there is no path for a TS file to embed a Claude instruction. The generator's output schema is the only way to talk to the API.
- **Code ↔ provider**: enforced by P1 — only `chain/adapter.py` knows which Claude provider is active. Skills name actions, not models.
- **Instruction ↔ runtime**: enforced by P6 — SKILL.md is markdown; runtime never embeds prompts. Editing a prompt is a content change, not a code change.

These boundaries are what make Phase 3 a one-week change rather than a refactor: each layer is replaceable in isolation because the seams are explicit.

## Related Documents

- [Analysis](./analysis.md) – Problems driving design
- [Epic](./epic.md) – Scope and tasks
- [Timeline](./timeline.md) – Status tracking
